name: Password Guessing (Brute Force)
description: Adversaries may guess passwords to gain access to target systems or valid accounts. In brute force password guessing, adversaries systematically try passwords from a dictionary or randomized list against an authentication service such as SSH, RDP, or web logins.
detection: Monitor authentication logs (e.g., /var/log/auth.log, /var/log/secure, Windows Event ID 4625) for high volumes of failed login attempts followed by a potential success from the same IP address.
mitigation: M1036 (Account Use Policies), M1032 (Multi-factor Authentication), M1037 (Filter Network Traffic - IP rate limiting / fail2ban / firewall dropping).

name: PowerShell Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution. PowerShell is a powerful interactive command-line interface and scripting environment. Attackers leverage encoded commands (-Enc, -EncodedCommand), download cradles (IEX, DownloadString), and hidden window execution flags (-W Hidden) to evade basic scrutiny.
detection: Enable and inspect PowerShell Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104), Module Logging (Event ID 4103), and Process Creation (Event ID 4688 / Sysmon Event 1) with CommandLine capture.
mitigation: M1038 (Execution Prevention - PowerShell Constrained Language Mode), M1026 (Privileged Account Management), M1049 (Antivirus/EDR behavior blocking).

name: Sudo and Sudo Caching (Abuse Elevation Control)
description: Adversaries may abuse sudo configuration or cached credentials to execute commands with elevated privileges (root). Attackers who compromise a low-privileged account (such as www-data or service accounts) may check sudo -l or exploit misconfigured sudoers rules or setuid binaries to read /etc/shadow or spawn a root shell.
detection: Audit sudo command history via auth.log, syslog, or auditd. Look for commands invoked with sudo by service/web accounts, or modifications to /etc/sudoers.
mitigation: M1026 (Privileged Account Management - restrict sudo access), M1028 (Operating System Configuration - enforce strict sudoers policies and NOPASSWD elimination).

name: Inhibit System Recovery
description: Adversaries may delete or remove built-in system recovery features, such as Volume Shadow Copies, backup catalogs, or boot configuration data, to prevent recovery after a ransomware deployment or destructive attack. Common commands include 'vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet' and 'wmic shadowcopy delete'.
detection: Monitor process execution logs (Sysmon Event 1, Windows Event 4688) for invocations of vssadmin.exe, wmic.exe, or bcdedit.exe with shadow deletion parameters.
mitigation: M1022 (Restrict File and Directory Permissions), M1018 (User Account Management - enforce least privilege), M1053 (Data Backup - immutable offline/cloud backups).

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit vulnerabilities in Internet-facing software (e.g., SQL Injection, Remote Code Execution in web applications, CMS exploits) to gain an initial foothold or exfiltrate sensitive backend database contents.
detection: Deploy Web Application Firewalls (WAF) and analyze web server access logs for anomalous SQL syntax, suspicious URI parameters, and high volume HTTP 500 error responses.
mitigation: M1050 (Exploit Protection), M1041 (Encrypt Sensitive Information), M1016 (Vulnerability Scanning & Input Sanitization/Prepared Statements).

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Compromised credentials may be used to log in legitimately via VPN or RDP without triggering malware alarms.
detection: Analyze user behavior analytics (UBA) for concurrent logins, impossible travel velocities, and logins from unexpected geographical locations or atypical off-hours.
mitigation: M1032 (Multi-factor Authentication), M1030 (Network Segmentation), M1018 (Account Management - periodic credential rotation and strict session timeouts).

name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
description: Adversaries may use SMB to interact with Windows Admin Shares (e.g., C$, ADMIN$) to remotely execute code and propagate laterally within a network using tools like PsExec or winexe.
detection: Monitor network traffic for anomalous SMB connections between workstations, and track Event ID 7045 (New Service Installed) or Event ID 5145 (Network Share Object Checked).
mitigation: M1035 (Limit Access to Resource Over Network - block port 445 between endpoints), M1026 (Privileged Account Management - disable Remote UAC and administrative shares where unnecessary).

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including port scanning (e.g. Nmap, Masscan, SYN scans) to identify exploitable listening daemons.
detection: Use Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS/Suricata/Snort) to detect rapid port sweeps and half-open SYN packets from a single source IP.
mitigation: M1030 (Network Segmentation), M1037 (Filter Network Traffic - stateful firewall drop rules and rate limiting).
